Re: Trump Goes for the Stoner Vote

Wall Street Journal Editorial page December 19, 2025

To the Wall Street Journal Editorial Board:

From Richard Cowan MarijuanaNews.com

December 26, 2025

I have been reading the Journal and its editorial pages for over sixty years (even longer than I have smoked “marijuana”), because I believe that it plays an important part in the capitalist system that upholds individual freedom… Except…

It was with great sadness and frustration that after a decade or so I eventually discovered that the Journal had rejected libertarianism in favor of a “reefer madness” level of Prohibitionism regarding cannabis.

 I remember when you printed an Oped by Milton Freedman once, calling for you to support freedom, but you ignored him, and Buckley, and Von Mises, and  George Shultz, Reason and Cato and all of your natural allies

Consequently, I have kept track of the occasional recrudescence of an intellectual level that is simply unworthy of any claim of seriousness. You seem rather busy these days.

 Consider:

The December 19, 2025 editorial headlined Trump Goes for The Stoner Vote

“Marijuananews note: The implication here is that anyone who favors even rescheduling cannabis is a “Stoner”, but as noted in the paragraph above, that includes many, if not most, of your strongest free market allies, and millions of older Americans. And do you really expect to be taken seriously saying,

“Rescheduling pot sends the wrong message to vulnerable young brains”???

Marijuananews: Do you really think that emotionally disturbed teens follow DEA Scheduling? “Hey Joe, I just read in The Wall Street Journal that weed has been moved from Schedule One to Schedule Three! That must mean that it is harmless like booze. They won’t sell it to us at the new Dispensary on Main Street, so let’s go see that guy in the alley. He says it’s harmless, like back in the 60s, before they arrested 30 million people.” 

Joe Biden sought to wave away student debt to attract young people. Now President Trump is making a play for the bro vote by relaxing federal regulations on marijuana. Can’t afford to buy a home? Don’t worry, dude. Puff away your economic anxieties in mom and dad’s basement.

Marijuananews note: Relevance??? Remember, this is about rescheduling cannabis for medical use. Dude??

See

Many Older Adults Use Cannabis for Health Reasons

And

Cannabis use is up 46% among American seniors as Trump signs an order to reclassify marijuana. Are you positioned to profit if pot stocks surge?

Yes, and no. Reclassifying marijuana under the Controlled Substances Act doesn’t legalize the drug under federal law. But it does let marijuana sellers deduct expenses from their taxes like other companies. It also sends the signal to young people that marijuana isn’t all that harmful, despite mounting evidence that it is. 

Marijuana is currently a Schedule I drug, meaning it has “no currently accepted medical use and a high potential for abuse.” Mr. Trump aims to change it to Schedule III—akin to anabolic steroids, indicating that it has some legitimate medical uses and “a moderate to low potential for physical and psychological dependence.”

Marijuananews

See



Marijuana Is In Schedule One. Fentanyl Is In Schedule 2. Think About It.

Doesn’t that mean that the current status tells teens that fentanyl is safer than marijuana?? And you are in favor of that??

Yet a recent review of 15 years of research found the evidence of marijuana’s medical benefits to be weak or inconclusive. “The evidence does not support the use of cannabis or cannabinoids at this point for most of the indications that folks are using it for,” said the study’s lead author Michael Hsu.

Marijuananews note: Well, not really!

The Journal did not publish a link to the study which got lots of publicity. It is behind a paywall but UCLA medical school has a summary

See

Evidence lacking for medical cannabis in most conditions

2 Dec 2025 — “For some conditions, our research found evidence that cannabis was not effective,” Hsu continued…

Dr. Michael     Hsu, the review’s first author and health sciences clinical instructor at the UCLA Health Department of Psychiatry and Biobehavioral Sciences, said, “In medical training, we just don't receive extensive education on the topic of medical cannabis. Many physicians lack comprehensive training on its benefits, risks and proper dosages, leading to confusion, and, at times, avoidance of the conversation altogether.”

Marijuananews: Exactly, the lead researcher is a psychiatrist, not an epidemiologist. Is there bias or disqualification?

See

There Is Absolutely No Scientific Basis For Politicized Psychiatry Determining Cannabis Policy

And

A Truly Great Report From The UK On The Problems That Both The Patients And The Police Have With Legal Medical Cannabis In Very Prohibitionist Country (And Unlikely To Be Reported In The US)

And

Anti Cannabis Bias In Medical Research And The Lone Research Paper That Told Them What They Didn’t Want to Hear

And

They Say The Brain Doesn’t Mature Until We Are 25 But That Doesn’t Stop The “Medical Profession” From Giving Children In Foster Care Powerful Psychiatric Drugs

Why doesn’t the Journal denounce this??

“Many physicians lack comprehensive training on its benefits, risks and proper dosages, leading to confusion, and, at times, avoidance of the conversation altogether.”

“The review confirmed that pharmaceutical-grade cannabinoids approved by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration have demonstrated effectiveness but only in a narrow range of conditions. These include medications for HIV/AIDS-related appetite loss, chemotherapy-induced nausea and vomiting…

and certain severe pediatric seizure disorders such as Dravet syndrome and Lennox-Gastaut syndrome.

Marijuananews:

See Marinol Was The First Schedule 2 Drug To Be "Down-Scheduled," Boasts Roxanne On Its New Marinol.com Web Site. Doesn’t That Mean That It Should Never Have Been Schedule 2 Anyway?….

Also See “Charlotte Figgi, died at the age of 13. If you use CBD, you should know her name and her story. From the time she was three months old she suffered from Dravet syndrome, a severe form of epilepsy that begins in infancy and often results in seizures every hour of every day. When she was five her parents discovered that CBD greatly reduced the frequency and severity of her seizures, so for the last eight years of her life she and her family had some semblance of normal lives.

Dr. Sanjay Gupta said, “She made me realize that it would not just be a medical failing but a moral failing if this medicine was somehow withheld from people.”

See

HOW GW PHARMA WON CBD

In short, all three of the FDA approved pharmaceuticals were “discovered” as a result of illegal marijuana use, without the formal involvement of the medical profession.

 

First, because marijuana is in Schedule One, it is very difficult to do research to find what NIDA does not want you to find.

See Cannabis research database shows how U.S. funding focuses on harms of the drug

27 Aug 2020 —  “A new analysis of cannabis research funding in the United States, Canada, and the United Kingdom has found that $1.56 billion was directed to the topic between 2000 and 2018—with about half of the money spent on understanding the potential harms of the recreational drug. Just over $1 billion came from the biggest funder, the U.S. National Institute on Drug Abuse (NIDA), which doled out far more money to research cannabis misuse and its negative effects than on using cannabis and cannabis-derived chemicals as a therapeutic drug.”

Far stronger evidence points to its potential harm. Mr. Trump may not realize that weed today is four to five times more potent than in the 1990s. The drug’s dangers and risks of dependency increase with potency. The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) estimates that about three in 10 people who use marijuana will develop an addiction.

A study this year found that 40% of car drivers who died in accidents in an Ohio county tested positive for THC, the psychoactive ingredient in marijuana.

Marijuananews note: The study did not say that the drivers had only THC and did not have alcohol and/or drugs in their blood. Also, note that people test positive for THC even after they are no longer impaired.

See

“Stoned Driver Tests” Seriously Flawed And Could Put Innocent People In Jail. Is That A Feature Or A Bug For Prohibitionists?

And

The Editorial Page of the Wall Street Journal Degrades Itself

and links

Marijuana advocates claim weed is no worse than alcohol. They ignore that cannabis has longer-term impact than alcohol, especially among the young.

Marijuananews:

See Alcohol-related dementia“ (ARD) is a form of dementia caused by long-term, excessive consumption of alcohol, resulting in neurological damage.”

And Alcohol Induced Deaths In The United States Increased by 89% from 1999 to 2024! Where Are The Headlines?

As the CDC says, “cannabis use directly affects the parts of the brain responsible for memory, learning, attention, decision-making, coordination, emotion, and reaction time.” Medical imaging of adolescent brains shows structural changes in areas involved in impulse control and decision-making.

It can cause psychotic symptoms, especially at higher potency. A bag of cannabis gummies can cause a bad trip for some users. The CDC this summer reported that at least 85 people who frequented a Wisconsin restaurant that had mistakenly used THC-infused oil in pizza dough experienced symptoms of cannabis intoxication. Nearly half of those who got sick suffered paranoia and a quarter hallucinated.

Marijuananews: So we should oppose medical cannabis in case an incompetent cook might accidentally overmedicate us?

The number of cannabis-related incidents reported to poison-control centers has surged 23-fold since 2009, mostly among teens and children.

Marijuananews: How many reported fatalities? Compared with prescription drugs, etc.)

As we reported last week, young pot users are showing up with rising frequency at emergency rooms with uncontrolled vomiting and psychotic symptoms. One study this year found young users had a sixfold higher risk of heart attacks and fourfold greater of strokes.

Marijuananews note: One study? Citation needed.

Yet the same Administration that targets Tylenol—which has proven benefits and minimal risks—now says marijuana is fine.

Marijuananews note: I have no opinion on “Tylenol” regulations, but…

See Acetaminophen toxicity

“Acetaminophen is one of the most commonly used analgesics and antipyretics. Although relatively safe at therapeutic doses, acetaminophen poisoning causes hepatic necrosis. Acetaminophen toxicity is the second most common cause of liver transplantation worldwide and the most common cause of liver failure in the United States. Responsible for 56,000 emergency department visits and 2600 hospitalizations, acetaminophen poisoning causes 500 deaths annually in the United States. Notably, around 50% of these poisonings are unintentional, often resulting from patients misinterpreting dosing instructions or unknowingly consuming multiple acetaminophen-containing products.”

The cannabis lobby claims rescheduling will allow more research on the drug, but the industry can run trials on marijuana now. It simply has no incentive to do so because it can sell its products in most states without Food and Drug Administration approval.

Marijuananews note: Huh? Pharmaceutical companies do tests to develop proprietary products that they patent. Surely the editors of the Wall Street Journal know this.

So why ease regulation on pot?  Occam’s razor says Mr. Trump wants to shore up support among young voters. On Thursday he volunteered that rescheduling polls well.

Marijuananews note: Democracy is bad when the peasants disagree with their betters on the Journal Editorial Board.

Is he sure? Ballot measures to legalize the drug for recreational use failed in South and North Dakota, Arkansas and Florida in recent years.

Marijuananews note: The subject is medical, not recreational, and the Dakotas and Arkansas are very conservative states.

In 2016, the Arkansas Medical Marijuana Amendment passed by a vote of 53%–47% as an amendment to the state constitution. It allows patients who obtain a doctor's recommendation to possess up to 21/2 ounces.

In November of last year, Trump voted for Florida’s recreational marijuana initiative, and it got 55% of the vote, but the state Constitution requires that an amendment to the state Constitution get 60% of the votes. Trump got around 56%.

Voters in Maine and Massachusetts have launched referenda campaigns to repeal legalization.

Marijuananews note: I’m so old that I can remember when Prohibitionists were against referendums about marijuana.

Pot smoking is a leading reason employers reject job applicants after drug tests.

Marijuananews note:

Really now?? Surely you know that THC is fat soluble, while all of the other illegal substances are water soluble. Consequently, cannabis is detectable for up to a month after last use, while cocaine cannot usually be detected for more than two days. So, naturally cannabis, which is more widely used than any other illegal substance, will be detected more often than other drugs. So, if you want your employees to use hard drugs, “drug test” them.

See

Why "Drug" Testing Is Really Just Marijuana Testing – Which Is Counterproductive

We’re not for punishing casual pot smokers. But sending a message to teens and 20-year-olds that marijuana is harmless is a recipe for more damaged brains and human tragedy.

Marijuananews note: Human tragedy?

What about thirty million arrests, most for simple possession, since the 1970s? And it is continuing even now at a rate of over two hundred thousand a year. Has the Journal ever urged decriminalizing simple possession?

Next week I will review the Journal’s actual record over the last 25 years.

In the meantime, here is a list of countries that have legalized medical use of cannabis, including Albania, Argentina, Australia, Barbados, Brazil, Canada, Chile, Colombia, Costa Rica, Croatia, Cyprus, Czech Republic, Denmark, Ecuador, Finland, Germany, Greece, Ireland, Israel, Italy, Jamaica, Lebanon, Luxembourg, Malawi, Malta, Mexico, the Netherlands, New Zealand, North Macedonia, Norway, Panama, Peru, Poland, Portugal, Rwanda, Saint Vincent and the Grenadines, San Marino, Slovenia, South Africa, Spain, Sri Lanka, Switzerland, Thailand, Ukraine, the United Kingdom, Uruguay, Vanuatu, Zambia, and Zimbabwe.

Are we here in the Land of the Free so unworthy?

Sincerely,

Richard Cowan
